query_text: how do you type up minutes of a meeting

parts.text:
Typing up meeting minutes is about creating an official, clear, and objective record of what happened, what was decided, and what actions need to be taken. It is **not** a word-for-word transcript, but rather a summary of key points.

Here is a step-by-step guide on how to type up professional meeting minutes, along with a reusable template.

---

### Step 1: Prepare Before the Meeting
The secret to writing great minutes is preparation. 
* **Get the Agenda:** Always ask for the meeting agenda beforehand. You can use the agenda items as your outline/headings to organize your notes.
* **Create a Template:** Set up your document in advance with the date, time, list of expected attendees, and the agenda topics.
* **Know the Goals:** Understand what the meeting is trying to achieve so you know which discussions are most important to document.

---

### Step 2: Take Smart Notes During the Meeting
Don't try to write down every word. Focus on capturing the following:
* **Decisions:** What was agreed upon? (e.g., "The board approved the Q3 budget.")
* **Action Items:** Who is doing what, and by when? (e.g., "John to email the revised proposal to the client by Friday, Oct 12.")
* **Key Arguments/Points:** Briefly note major points of discussion, especially if there was a debate, but keep it high-level. 
* **Next Steps:** Note when and where the next meeting will take place.

---

### Step 3: Type Up the Minutes (The Final Draft)
Write or polish the minutes as soon as possible after the meeting while your memory is fresh. Keep these rules in mind:

* **Use a Professional Tone:** Write in a clear, neutral, and objective third-person perspective (e.g., "The committee discussed..." instead of "We talked about...").
* **Avoid Personal Opinions:** Do not include personal interpretations, emotional descriptions, or side comments (e.g., write "A discussion ensued regarding the budget," not "Sarah got angry about the budget").
* **Keep it Concise:** Use bullet points and bold text to make the document highly scannable. 
* **Clarify Action Items:** Bold the names of people responsible for tasks so they stand out when people skim the document.

---

### Standard Meeting Minutes Template

You can copy, paste, and fill out this standard template for your meeting:

```text
[ORGANIZATION OR TEAM NAME]
MEETING MINUTES

Date: [Date of the meeting]
Time: [Start Time] to [End Time]
Location: [Conference Room, Zoom, Teams, etc.]
Meeting Chair: [Name of the person running the meeting]
Minute-Taker: [Your Name]

1. ATTENDEES
• Present: [Name 1], [Name 2], [Name 3]
• Apologies/Absent: [Name 4], [Name 5]
• Guests: [Name, Title, if applicable]

2. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MINUTES
• The minutes of the previous meeting held on [Date] were [approved as distributed / approved with the following corrections: ...].

3. AGENDA ITEMS & DISCUSSION
• Topic 1: [Name of Topic]
  - [Brief summary of the discussion, main points raised, and conclusions reached.]
  - Decision: [Document any official decisions made.]
  
• Topic 2: [Name of Topic]
  - [Brief summary of the discussion...]
  - Decision: [Document any official decisions made.]

4. ACTION ITEMS (Who, What, When)
• [Name] to [Action Item/Task] by [Deadline/Due Date].
• [Name] to [Action Item/Task] by [Deadline/Due Date].

5. OTHER BUSINESS (Varia / Round-table)
• [Note any unexpected topics brought up at the end of the meeting that weren't on the agenda.]

6. NEXT MEETING
• Date: [Date of next meeting]
• Time: [Time]
• Location: [Location]

7. ADJOURNMENT
• The meeting was adjourned at [End Time] by [Name of Chair].

Minutes submitted by: [Your Name, Signature]
Minutes approved by: [Chair’s Name, Signature]
```

---

### Step 4: Review and Distribute
1. **Proofread:** Check for spelling, grammatical errors, and clarity. Ensure all names are spelled correctly.
2. **Get Approval (If Required):** Send a draft to the meeting chair or facilitator first. They may want to review it for accuracy before it is sent to the wider group.
3. **Distribute Promptly:** Aim to send the minutes within **24 to 48 hours** of the meeting. This keeps action items fresh in everyone’s minds. Attach any documents or presentations that were shared during the meeting to the distribution email.
